findings_addressed.oracle: ProviderName.LOCAL_TRANSFORMERS.value (the enum's string value declared in intellicrack/core/types.py) must equal the literal string 'local_transformers' that is hard-coded into the logger-bind call at local_transformers.py line 202. These are two separate source locations; neither is derived from the other in the test. Additionally, the test re-derives the logger context dict from the bound logger and asserts both the enum value and the logger field equal the same independent constant.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/core/types.py, change LOCAL_TRANSFORMERS = "local_transformers" to LOCAL_TRANSFORMERS = "transformers_local"; the assertion `assert ProviderName.LOCAL_TRANSFORMERS.value == expected_label` fails immediately because the enum value no longer equals the expected label string.

notes: G0276 was a no-assertion finding: the original test only checked `provider.name == ProviderName.LOCAL_TRANSFORMERS`, which is a tautology (the property returns exactly that enum member). The hardened version asserts `ProviderName.LOCAL_TRANSFORMERS.value == 'local_transformers'` (independent oracle: the string value in the enum declaration vs the hard-coded string in the logger binding) and additionally re-validates that the bound logger context field equals the same expected label, ensuring any desynchronisation between the enum string and the logger-bind literal is caught.
